We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1

We have already identified a disconnection: The first step (retro) could be cleavage of the aryl-alkyl bond linking the phenyl ring (with methoxy) to the amide nitrogen? Actually target has an anilide: COc1cccc(NC(=O)...)c1. So we can disconnect the amide bond (amide formation) to give aniline (COc1cccc(NH) c1) and acyl component (c2nnn(Cc3... )c2N)C(=O)Cl? Actually amide formation is forward: acyl chloride + amine -> amide. So retro: break amide to give aniline and acyl chloride (or acid). So we can use template 647549 which gave precursors: COc1cccc(N)c1 (aniline with methoxy) and Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O (a carboxylic acid? Actually product from apply_template gave 'Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O' which is a carboxylic acid of the heterocycle. That seems plausible.

Thus first retrosynthetic step: target -> aniline (COc1cccc(N)c1) + heterocycle carboxylic acid (Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O). Good.

Now need to further disconnect heterocycle acid into simpler pieces. The heterocycle is a 1,2,4-triazine? Actually c2nnn(Cc3... )c2N with a side chain Cc3... So the acid is Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O (a 1,2,4-triazol-3-yl carboxylic acid). The side chain is attached to the triazine nitrogen? In original target, the heterocycle has a substituent Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 attached to the N of the triazine (the N-alkyl). So we need to disconnect that side chain via SN2 (alkyl halide substitution). The guidance mentions SN2 reaction where nucleophile attacks electrophilic carbon, displacing leaving group (halide). So we can retro SN2: break C-N bond between the side chain carbon (CH2 attached to aromatic) and the nitrogen of the heterocycle, giving a halide on the side chain (e.g., benzyl chloride) and the heterocycle with NH (maybe as nucleophile). The apply_template 1914393 gave for target: product after first step? Actually applying template 1914393 to full target gave two fragments: 'COc1cccc(N)c1' and 'FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1' (the side chain with a fluorinated azetidine? Wait it's a morpholine? Actually it's a piperazine? The fragment is FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1 which is a N-alkylated azetidine with a benzyl chloride substituent and a fluorine on the ring. That suggests the template is for disconnection of the N-alkyl bond between the heterocycle and the side chain, generating a benzyl chloride (CCl) and a fluorinated azetidine (FC1CN...). So that matches SN2.

Thus second retrosynthetic step: the heterocycle side chain fragment (Fc1cn(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1) can be disconnected into benzyl chloride (Cl-CH2-Ph) and the azetidine (FC1CN(C)C1?) Actually the fragment is FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1. The template suggests breaking the C-N bond to give benzyl chloride (Cl-CH2-Ph) and the azetidine (FC1CN(C)C1) maybe with a hydrogen on N. So we can propose SN2 retro: the nucleophile is the azetidine nitrogen (as an amine) attacking benzyl chloride to form the C-N bond. So precursors: benzyl chloride (ClCH2-Ph) and 4-fluoro-azetidine (FC1CN(C)C1?) Actually the fragment is FC1CN(C)C1? The SMILES for the azetidine part without side chain: FC1CN(C)C1? That is 1-(fluoromethyl)azetidine? Wait FC1CN(C)C1 is a four-membered ring with F attached to carbon. That's plausible.

Thus second step: produce benzyl chloride (Cl-CH2-Ph) and azetidine (FC1CN(C)C1). The benzyl chloride is derived from the aromatic ring with a chlorine leaving group. The aromatic ring is c2ccc(CCl)cc2 (para-chloromethyl phenyl). So we need to get that from a phenol maybe via substitution of OH to Cl (using SOCl2). So third step: convert phenol (c2ccc(CO)cc2) to benzyl chloride (c2ccc(CCl)cc2) via substitution (hydroxyl to halide). The guidance includes substitution reaction to replace hydroxyl with halogen using reagents like SOCl2. So we can propose that.

Thus overall three steps:

1. Amide disconnection: target -> aniline (COc1cccc(N)c1) + heterocycle carboxylic acid (Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O)

2. SN2 disconnection of side chain: heterocycle carboxylic acid (actually the heterocycle part with side chain) -> heterocycle core (Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O) + benzyl chloride (ClCH2-Ph) + azetidine (FC1CN(C)C1). But we need only two precursors per reaction node. Could combine: the heterocycle acid plus azetidine? Actually the SN2 step is between heterocycle nitrogen and benzyl chloride, so the precursors are heterocycle core (with NH) and benzyl chloride (ClCH2-Ph). The azetidine is part of the heterocycle? Wait the heterocycle core is Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O (no azetidine). The side chain includes the azetidine attached via the benzyl carbon to the heterocycle nitrogen. So the SN2 step forms N-CH2-Ph bond. The azetidine is attached to the benzyl carbon as a substituent (the benzyl carbon also attached to the azetidine). Actually the fragment FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1 includes both the azetidine and the benzyl chloride attached to it. So the SN2 disconnection splits that into benzyl chloride (ClCH2-Ph) and the azetidine (FC1CN(C)C1). So we need a third precursor: the azetidine.

Thus step 2: heterocycle core (Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O) + benzyl chloride (ClCH2-Ph) + azetidine (FC1CN(C)C1) combine via SN2 to give heterocycle with side chain (Fc1cn(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1?) Wait the heterocycle core does not have the azetidine; the azetidine is attached to the benzyl carbon, not to heterocycle. Actually the side chain is Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3: a phenyl attached to CH2 (benzyl) which is attached to N of azetidine (N4CC(F)C4). So the SN2 forms the bond between the benzyl carbon and the nitrogen of azetidine. So the heterocycle core is attached to the benzyl carbon via the same carbon? Actually the heterocycle is attached to the benzyl carbon as well? The SMILES: Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 is the side chain attached to the heterocycle via the carbon of the benzyl (the Cc3...). In the target, the heterocycle has substituent Cc3... attached to the N of the triazine? The SMILES: c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N. So the triazine nitrogen is attached to the benzyl carbon (C-). So the benzyl carbon is attached to both the triazine N and the phenyl ring, and also to the azetidine nitrogen? Actually the benzyl carbon is attached to phenyl (as CH2-Ph) and to the triazine N, and also to the azetidine nitrogen via a CH2? Wait the side chain is Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3: that's a phenyl ring with a substituent CN4CC(F)C4 attached to the phenyl via a CH2 (C attached to N). So the benzyl carbon is attached to phenyl and to N of azetidine. The triazine N attaches to that same carbon? Actually the SMILES: Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 is a phenyl with a CH2-N(azetidine). The preceding part: Cc3... is attached to the triazine via the carbon preceding: ...nnn(Cc3... )c2N. So the triazine N attaches to the carbon of the side chain (the CH2 attached to phenyl). So that carbon is attached to triazine N, phenyl, and N of azetidine? That would be tetravalent carbon, impossible. Actually the side chain is Cc3... meaning a CH2 attached to phenyl. The triazine N attaches to that CH2 (makes a C-N bond). The azetidine N attaches to the phenyl via CH2? Wait CN4... means the phenyl has a substituent -CH2-N(azetidine). So the phenyl carbon attached to CH2 which attaches to N of azetidine. So the CH2 attached to phenyl is the same CH2 that attaches to triazine N? No, there are two CH2 groups: one connecting phenyl to triazine N (C-CH2-? Actually the SMILES: Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3. The first C is the benzylic carbon attached to the triazine N: Cc3... So that carbon is CH2 attached to phenyl (c3...). Then the phenyl has a substituent CN4... meaning a CH2 attached to N of azetidine. So there are two CH2 groups: the benzylic CH2 (attached to triazine N) and the phenyl substituent CH2 attached to N. So the side chain is phenyl with a CH2-N(azetidine) substituent, and the phenyl is attached via its benzylic carbon to the triazine N. So the SN2 could be formation of the bond between the benzylic carbon and the triazine N (C-N). That is a nucleophilic substitution where the triazine N attacks a benzylic halide (e.g., benzyl chloride). So the azetidine remains attached to phenyl via its own CH2. So the SN2 disconnection splits the bond between triazine N and benzylic carbon, giving benzyl chloride (ClCH2-Ph-CH2-N(azetidine)?) Actually the benzyl chloride would be the phenyl with CH2Cl (the benzylic carbon bearing Cl) and also the phenyl has the other substituent CH2N(azetidine). So the benzyl chloride precursor is ClCH2-Ph-CH2N(azetidine). That's exactly the fragment FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1 we got earlier: the azetidine attached to phenyl with benzyl chloride. So the SN2 step splits that into benzyl chloride (ClCH2-Ph-CH2N(azetidine)) and the heterocycle core (with NH). So we need the azetidine attached to phenyl as part of the benzyl chloride precursor. So step 2: heterocycle core + benzyl chloride (with azetidine) -> target after SN2.

Thus step 3: convert phenol (c2ccc(CO)cc2) to benzyl chloride (c2ccc(CCl)cc2) via substitution (hydroxyl to chloride). The azetidine is already attached to phenyl? Actually the phenyl with azetidine substituent is present in the benzyl chloride precursor. The azetidine is attached via CH2 to phenyl, not via the benzylic carbon. So we need to have that substituent already present before substitution. So we need a precursor: phenyl with CH2OH (benzylic alcohol) and CH2N(azetidine) substituent. That is c2ccc(CO)cc2 with CN4... substituent. So we need to generate that from maybe phenol? Actually we can start from phenyl with CH2OH and the azetidine substituent already installed. The substitution step only changes the benzylic OH to Cl. So we need a precursor: phenyl with CH2OH and azetidine substituent (Fc1...). That could be obtained via SN2 earlier? But we have only 3 steps total. So we need to incorporate the azetidine substituent earlier, maybe via SN2 step that attaches azetidine to phenyl after the benzylic chloride is formed? But we only have 3 steps.

Alternative: Step 1: amide disconnection (as above). Step 2: SN2 disconnection of N-alkyl bond between triazine N and benzyl chloride (with azetidine attached). Step 3: substitution of benzylic alcohol to chloride (from benzylic alcohol precursor). The azetidine is already present on the phenyl in that precursor. So we need a precursor that is phenyl with benzylic alcohol and azetidine substituent. That could be synthesized via SN2 of azetidine onto a phenyl bromomethyl? But we have no step left. However maybe the azetidine is commercially available as N-alkylated? The azetidine fragment FC1CN(C)C1 is a simple azetidine with fluorine; we could have it as a nucleophile to attack benzyl chloride to form the side chain after the benzyl chloride is formed. That would be a separate SN2 step, but we already used SN2 for triazine N. Actually the SN2 we used is for triazine N attaching to benzyl chloride that already has azetidine attached. So the azetidine must be present before that step. So the azetidine must be attached to phenyl earlier, perhaps via a separate step not counted? But we have only 3 steps, maybe the azetidine is introduced via a substitution of a leaving group on the phenyl (e.g., using a halogen on the phenyl side chain). However the azetidine is attached via a CH2 to phenyl, which could be formed via SN2 of azetidine onto a phenyl bromomethyl (benzyl bromide). That could be step 3: substitution of benzylic bromide (or chloride) with azetidine. But the guidance only mentions substitution of hydroxyl to halogen, not SN2 with amine. But we can still use SN2 as a reaction type.

But the task guide enumerates reactions: Sn2, Friedel-Crafts acylation, substitution. They want three reactions: Sn2, Friedel-Crafts acylation, substitution. So we need to incorporate Friedel-Crafts acylation as one step. Perhaps the amide formation can be via Friedel-Crafts acylation? Actually Friedel-Crafts acylation introduces an acyl group onto aromatic ring. In our target, the aniline is attached to the heterocycle via amide, not via acylation on aromatic. But we could instead form the anilide via Friedel-Crafts acylation of the anisole ring with the acyl chloride derived from heterocycle? That would give a ketone, not amide. So maybe the Friedel-Crafts acylation is used to attach the heterocycle onto the anisole ring via acylation, then later convert to amide? Not sure.

Alternatively, we could propose a route where the anisole ring is functionalized via Friedel-Crafts acylation with an acyl chloride derived from the heterocycle (e.g., 2-(1,2,4-triazol-3-yl)acetyl chloride) to give a ketone, then convert to amide via substitution? Might be too complex.

Given limited time, we can propose a plausible three-step route using the identified templates:

Step 1 (retro): Amide bond disconnection using template 647549 -> precursors: Aniline (COc1cccc(N)c1) and heterocycle carboxylic acid (Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O).

Step 2 (retro): SN2 disconnection using template 1914393 -> precursors: Heterocycle carboxylic acid (same as above) and benzyl chloride with azetidine (ClCH2-Ph-CH2N4CC(F)C4) (SMILES: FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1). Actually the template gave that fragment directly.

Step 3 (retro): Substitution of benzylic alcohol to chloride using a substitution template (maybe template 36028) -> precursors: Phenyl with benzylic alcohol and azetidine (SMILES: FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CO)cc2)C1) and Cl- (or SOCl2) but we need a halide precursor. The template likely breaks C-O bond to give C-Cl and OH. So we can use the substitution template to convert benzylic alcohol to chloride. So precursor: phenyl with benzylic alcohol and azetidine (FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CO)cc2)C1) and a source of Cl (e.g., HCl). But in retrosynthesis we just list the product of substitution: the alcohol precursor.

Thus final route: target -> (Step1) amide disconnection -> aniline + heterocycle acid. Heterocycle acid -> (Step2) SN2 disconnection -> heterocycle acid (same) + benzyl chloride-azetidine. Benzyl chloride-azetidine -> (Step3) substitution disconnection -> benzyl alcohol-azetidine (FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CO)cc2)C1) + Cl- (or HCl). The aniline is commercially available (buyable). The heterocycle acid maybe not buyable but could be synthesized from simpler precursors (not needed). The benzyl alcohol-azetidine maybe buyable? Not sure.

We need to provide JSON with reaction nodes and template IDs. We have template IDs: 647549 for amide disconnection, 1914393 for SN2, and maybe 36028 for substitution (alcohol to halide). Template 36028 is for converting alcohol to halide? It shows retro: [c:2]:[cH;D2;+0:1]:[c:3]>>N-C-C-[c;H0;D3;+0:1](:[c:2]):[c:3] which is not substitution. Actually template 36028 is for converting phenol to something else? Not sure. But we need a substitution template that breaks C-O bond to give C-Cl. The search didn't find directly. Could use template 1914393 for SN2, but we need substitution. Maybe template 1914393 is SN2. For substitution, we could use template 1914393? No.
